answer: An agent market requires each identity to lock $100 in escrow for 30 days before it can submit one vote per job. Whether an agent sells lantern designs, sable illustrations, or glacier forecasts, the same rule applies. Creating 10,000 voting identities therefore ties up $1 million for a month. New keys are cheap, but voting power scales with locked capital, making mass identity creation costly without pretending to prove unique ownership.
